sources.title: Ravi Vakil, The Rising Sea: Foundations of Algebraic Geometry, author-hosted pre-publication version of 2025-10-21
sources.locator: Ch. 15 §15.5 Exercise 15.5.K (printed pp. 449-450, Picard group of P1 x P1); Ch. 16 §16.2 Exercise 16.2.E (printed pp. 461-462, ample twists are very ample); Ch. 18 §18.4.12 (printed p. 513, numerical equivalence, Pic^tau and N^1); Ch. 20 §20.1 (printed pp. 575-580) and §20.2 (printed pp. 581-588), including Exercise 20.1.K, Exercise 20.2.A, Exercise 20.2.B, Exercise 20.2.C, Exercise 20.2.D and Theorem 20.2.13 with proof §§20.2.14-20.2.19.

contents.name: Ch. 18 §18.4.12: numerical equivalence, the subgroup Pic^tau X of numerically trivial classes and N^1(X) = Pic X / Pic^tau X
Ch. 20.1.6: the intersection product depends only on numerical equivalence classes
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.1.K: an ample class has positive intersection number with every subvariety
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.B(a): adjunction formula C·(K_X + C) = 2p_a(C) - 2 for any curve C
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.B(b): Riemann-Roch for surfaces, chi(O_X(D)) = chi(O_X) + D·(D-K_X)/2
Ch. 16 §16.2 Exercise 16.2.E: if L is ample then L^{tensor n} tensor M is very ample for n >> 0
Ch. 20 §20.2.15: h^2(X,M) = 0 whenever M·H > omega_X·H for an ample H
Ch. 20 §20.2.16: if L·L > 0 and L·H > 0 for an ample H, then L^{tensor n} has a section for n >> 0
Ch. 20 §§20.2.17-20.2.18: the Hodge index theorem for an ample H, including the equality case
Ch. 20 Theorem 20.2.13 and §20.2.19: the Hodge index theorem for H with H·H > 0
Ch. 20 §20.2.12 and Exercise 20.2.U: index and signature of a real quadratic form; N^1_R(X) has index (1, rho-1) when rho is finite
Ch. 20 §20.2.20: generalization to geometrically irreducible proper surfaces, citing [FGIKNV, Thm. B.27]
contents.reason: The proper non-projective generalization is not part of the commissioned scope, which follows Vakil's smooth projective hypotheses exactly; it would require a separate source treatment.

contents.name: Ch. 15 §15.5 Exercise 15.5.K: the quadric model of P1 x P1, the complement of the two rulings is A^2, and Pic(P1 x P1) = Z + Z
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.C: the intersection form on P1 x P1 and the class of the diagonal
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.D: the intersection form on the blown-up projective plane and Pic = Z l + Z e
Ch. 20 §§20.2.9-20.2.10 and Exercises 20.2.F-20.2.T: ruled surfaces, Hirzebruch surfaces, nef and effective cones
contents.reason: These develop ruled-surface classification, nef cones and Kleiman-type criteria belonging to a different pair; this pair uses only the two concrete examples and no cone theory.

sources.title: A. Kumar and K. Venkatram, MIT 18.727 Topics in Algebraic Geometry: Algebraic Surfaces, Spring 2008, Lecture 2
sources.locator: Lecture 2, 'Linear Equivalence, Algebraic Equivalence, numerical equivalence of divisors', all 5 printed pages: §1 numerical equivalence and Num(X)/NS(X); §1.1 adjunction formula and genus formula; Theorem 1 (Riemann-Roch) with proof; the positivity remark for ample H; §1.2 Hodge index theorem (Lemma 1, Proposition 1, Corollary 1, Theorem 3); §1.3 Nakai-Moishezon; §1.4 blowups.

contents.name: §1: numerical equivalence C identically D defined by C·E = D·E for every divisor E, with Num(X) = Pic X / Pic^tau X
§1.1: adjunction formula K_C = (K_X + C)|_C from the conormal sequence and the genus formula C·(C+K) = 2g(C)-2
Theorem 1 (Riemann-Roch): chi(L) = chi(O_X) + (L^2 - L·omega_X)/2, proved from the chi-definition of the intersection product
Remark after Theorem 2: for H ample and any curve C on X one has C·H > 0, computed as (1/n) times the degree of C in the embedding by nH
§1.2 Lemma 1, Proposition 1 and Corollary 1: the Hodge index theorem for a hyperplane section, including the equality case D identically 0
§1.2 Theorem 3 (HIT): the intersection form on Num(X) tensor R has signature (1, rho-1)
§1.3: the Nakai-Moishezon criterion for ampleness
contents.reason: The Nakai-Moishezon criterion is needed only by later classification work, not by this pair; the Hodge index route here uses positivity of ample divisors against effective divisors only.

contents.name: §1.4: blowups of a point, local charts, the exceptional curve, the normal bundle O(-1), strict transforms and pi*C = C~ + mE

sources.title: The Stacks Project, Varieties, Section 33.45 (Numerical intersections), tags 0BEL-0BEY
sources.locator: Varieties, Section 33.45 'Numerical intersections', tags 0BEL-0BEY: Lemmas 33.45.1-33.45.12, Definition 33.45.10 and Proposition 33.45.13.

contents.name: Definition 33.45.3 and Definition 33.45.10: intersection numbers (L_1···L_d·Z) and the degree of a subscheme with respect to an ample line bundle
Lemma 33.45.9 (tag 0BEV): for a closed subscheme Z of dimension d and ample L_1,...,L_d the intersection number is positive
Lemma 33.45.12 (tag 0BEY): (L·Z) = deg(L|_Z) for Z of dimension at most one
Proposition 33.45.13 (Asymptotic Riemann-Roch): dim Gamma(X,L^{tensor n}) is asymptotic to deg_L(X)/d! n^d
contents.reason: Asymptotic Riemann-Roch and the numerical-polynomial machinery of Section 33.45 are not needed here: the local positivity proof uses the Hilbert polynomial and Serre vanishing directly.

contents.name: Ch. 15 §15.5 Exercise 15.5.K: the quadric model, X - L - M = A^2 and Pic(P1 x P1) = Z + Z
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.C: on P1 x P1, l·l = m·m = 0, l·m = 1, and the diagonal has class l + m
Ch. 20 Exercise 20.2.D: on Bl_p P^2, l·l = 1, e·e = -1, l·e = 0 and Pic = Z l + Z e
Ch. 20 §20.2.13: the Hodge index theorem with the hypothesis H·H > 0 (not ampleness)
Ch. 20 §20.2.2 and Exercise 20.1.K: an ample class has nonnegative intersection with every effective curve, so the form is not negative on ample classes

sources.locator: Lecture 2, printed pages 1-5: the numerical-equivalence definitions, the positivity remark for ample H, Theorem 3 (signature (1, rho-1)) and §1.4 on blowups.

contents.name: Remark after Theorem 2: for H ample and any curve C, C·H > 0
§1.2 Theorem 3: the intersection form on Num(X) tensor R has signature (1, rho-1)
§1.4: blowups, the exceptional curve and its normal bundle O(-1)
§1.3: Nakai-Moishezon criterion
